concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: תְּפִלָּה (prayer) — central topic of the teaching but not used in any bechina declaration
כַּוָּנָה (intention/focus) — discussed as the goal of praying small portions, no bechina pairing
גִּלְגּוּל (reincarnation) — mentioned as a framework for why one may need to fix only certain prayer portions, no bechina
גֵּר (convert) — used as an analogy for appreciating small prayer accomplishments, not a bechina identity
בָּרוּךְ שֶׁאָמַר (Baruch She'amar) — a liturgical milestone used as an example starting point, not a bechina
מָארֵי דְּיָדַיִן / מָארֵי דְּרַגְלִין (masters of hands / masters of feet) — Zoharic concept that each person rectifies a different limb/portion of prayer, not presented as a bechina identity
analysis_notes.summary: This is a short, pastoral sicha-style teaching focused on encouragement for those who struggle with prayer. The Rebbe uses practical advice and analogies (the convert, gilgul, small portions) to help people not despair. The single appearance of the root בחינ in the text ('לפי בחינתו') means 'according to his level' — a common idiomatic usage, not a structural bechina declaration equating concepts. The teaching's logic is entirely eitza-type: breaking prayer into small portions LEADS TO ability to pray with kavanna; thinking of gilgul LEADS TO motivation. No bechina identities are declared, so no packages can be formed.
